description:
Accepted manual/forensic benchmark qualification decisions, loaded only through `--qualification-registry`. This is an INPUT contract, never a run artifact.

What a registry record may say is deliberately narrow. It supplies repository representativeness, the evidence and adjudication provenance behind that verdict, and at most a MORE RESTRICTIVE admission ceiling. It may not supply `usable_metric_families`, `benchmark_usability`, or `repository_level_comparison_eligible`: those are derived after exact matching against the authoritative measurement result, and accepting them here would create a second, unreconciled authority for facts `analysis.json` already owns. `additionalProperties: false` at every level is what enforces that - a registry that tries to supply a derived value is REJECTED rather than quietly ignored, because silent ignoring is indistinguishable from acceptance to whoever wrote the file.

A non-UNRESOLVED verdict requires accepted human or forensic-audit provenance. No automatic rule over extension counts, byte ratios, language labels, directory names or project markers may produce one; automated evidence may prepare or rank a decision but never replace it.

registry_schema_version.description: Version of this registry contract. Independent of Artifact Schema: a registry is an input, and its shape does not move when a run bundle's does.

source_id.description: Stable logical identifier for this registry, recorded in the run manifest so a decision can be traced to the file that carried it. Never an absolute workstation path.

qualification_profile.description: The question every record in this registry answers. A representativeness verdict is meaningless without it, so it is part of the primary binding rather than metadata.

records.description: Accepted decisions. Uniqueness of the primary binding is enforced by the loader, which reports a duplicate as a fatal registry error rather than choosing a winner.

title: ArchLens benchmark qualification registry 1.0

registry_record.description: One accepted qualification decision for one exactly-identified analyzed revision and scope.

record_id.description: Stable identifier for this decision, carried into the artifact and the checked projections.

repository_representativeness.description: Whether the selected supported scope adequately represents first-party application code for the declared profile. UNRESOLVED is an explicit state, never a default, and never silently upgraded.

representativeness_reason_codes.description: Stable semantic codes for the verdict. At least one is required for any non-UNRESOLVED decision; the loader enforces that, because a schema minItems cannot express the dependency on the enum.

manual_admission_restriction.description: An optional ceiling that can only make admission MORE restrictive. It can never promote a record: derived usability is computed first from measurement state and representativeness, and this may then lower it. `unsupported_scope` is an explicit editorial decision about the benchmark subject, not an automatic alias for NON_REPRESENTATIVE.

representativeness_basis.description: Human-readable evidence text. NON-SEMANTIC: it may clarify a decision but can never change one, and no gate, join, count or comparison may key on it.

usability_basis.description: Human-readable admission text. NON-SEMANTIC, exactly as `representativeness_basis`.

binding.description:
The primary identity of a qualification decision, and the whole of it. A decision is about one profile's question, asked of one subject, at one exact revision, over one exact analyzed scope.

`filesystem_manifest_hash` is deliberately ABSENT. The current contract describes it as broader filesystem evidence rather than comparability identity, so admitting it here would let a decision match or fail to match for reasons unrelated to what was measured.

subject_key.description: Logical subject identity. The join key across runs, revisions and source modes.

analyzed_commit_sha.description: The exact revision the decision was made about. A decision for one revision is not evidence about another.

analysis_scope_hash.description: Identity of the exact measured source scope.

analysis_scope_hash_version.description: Construction version of the scope hash. Two hashes built by different constructions are not comparable identities, so this is part of the key rather than an annotation.

evidence_summary.description: The evidence the accepted decision rests on. Counts and bytes are recorded on both sides; derived shares are NOT stored, because a stored ratio is a second copy of a fact that can drift from the numbers it came from. Consumers calculate shares.

unsupported_language_groups.description: Unsupported first-party language evidence. Required to be non-empty by the loader when unsupported first-party code exists.

project_or_service_structure_evidence_co.description: Structural assessment result. An explicit 0 means 'assessed, none found', which is a different fact from an absent assessment - and absence is refused for a non-UNRESOLVED record.

definition_mapped_code_line_evidence.description: OPTIONAL independent definition-mapped line evidence. Its absence is never zero: an empty list means no suitable independent tool and mapping existed, not that no code lines exist.

full_tree_evidence_sha256.description: Hash of the exact-tree evidence the decision was adjudicated against. Corroborates the decision; never replaces the primary binding.

evidence_source_ids.description: Stable logical evidence IDs, never absolute workstation paths.

adjudication.description: Provenance of the accepted decision. `mode` is constrained to human or accepted-forensic review: there is no enum member for an automatic rule, which is how the 'no automatic ADEQUATE' guarantee is expressed in the contract rather than only in the loader.

representativeness_reason_code.description: Adding or changing a member is a qualification-contract change, not a data edit.
